salut.consejo: The final t is not pronounced. The French u is said by rounding your lips as for «oo» while saying «ee».

je.consejo: The French «j» sounds like the «s» in «pleasure».

trad.en: you (on its own or for emphasis)
me (on its own or for emphasis)
pleased to meet you (said by a man)

enchantée.consejo: It sounds the same as the masculine form; only the spelling changes.

trad.en: pleased to meet you (said by a woman)

parents.consejo: Same as in English: the parents, not relatives.

fils.consejo: Here the s is pronounced and the l is not.

trad.en: his; her (before a feminine singular noun)
I get up; he/she gets up
in the evening (depending on the time)
have lunch; «on déjeune» = we have lunch
to postpone; to change the date
I don't like; he/she doesn't like

œufs.consejo: In the singular, «un œuf», the f is pronounced; in the plural, «œufs» is pronounced without the f or the final s. In «les œufs» you hear a linking «z» sound between the two words.

trad.en: it is needed; you have to
this, that (masculine before a vowel or silent h)

ou.consejo: Without the accent it means «or»; with the accent, «où», it means «where». They sound the same.

trad.en: how do you get to work?

autrefois.consejo: It is used to start telling something from the past.

j'habitais.consejo: It comes from «habiter» (to live). With «je», it is written with an apostrophe.

j'étais.consejo: The stem of «être» in the imperfect is «ét-».

j'aimais.consejo: It comes from «aimer» (to like, to love).

joue.consejo: In the present, the «I» form is «je joue».

trad.en: I play, you play, he/she plays

joué.consejo: Past participle of «jouer», used with «avoir» in the passé composé.

beau.consejo: In «il fait beau», it means the weather is nice.

arrivé.consejo: It takes «être»: je suis arrivé, elle est arrivée.

fera.consejo: «Il fera beau»: the weather will be nice.

s'il.consejo: It goes before a verb: s'il fait, s'il veut.

projets.consejo: Plural of «projet» (project). The -s is not heard.

mal.consejo: Used with «avoir mal»: to have pain.

pieds.consejo: Plural of «pied»: the -s is not heard.

aux.consejo: It is used before a plural: aux pieds, aux yeux.

gâteaux.consejo: Plural of «gâteau»: the -x is not heard.

faut.consejo: It comes from «il faut», which expresses obligation.

y.consejo: It replaces a place already mentioned.

ta.consejo: It is used before a feminine noun: ta sœur.

trad.en: your (possessive, with a feminine thing or person)

en (pronombre).consejo: It is not «en» (place): it replaces «de» + thing.

pull.consejo: A knitted garment for the top half.

bonne.consejo: It goes with a feminine noun: une bonne idée.

meilleur.consejo: Adjective: it agrees with the noun.

patron.consejo: For a man or a woman: the boss.

interdit.consejo: «Il est interdit de fumer» = no smoking.

parti.consejo: With «être», the past participle agrees with the subject.

trad.en: I was coming; you were coming

mode.consejo: There is the indicative, subjunctive, imperative...

trad.en: to offer; to give as a gift
to lead to; to bring about
quite the contrary; not at all
to meet; to get to know
there is no choice but to note
